notes: This minor release requires Bifrost 0.15.1 or later, as rules 0.11.0 did, and depends exactly on bifrost.public.packs 0.12.0. It adds one opt-in policy and fixes two false-positive patterns; no policy ID or required capability of an existing policy changes. New in bifrost.security 2.4.0: bifrost.security.python.process-input-to-venv-create (CVE-2024-9287, the version-independent part) reports process input that reaches the env_dir argument of venv.create (#355, #373). It needs the packs 0.12.0 venv models, and its required capabilities are all advertised by Bifrost 0.15.1. It is opt-in for the same reasons as the other Python process-input policies: a process input read after any modeled call is not selected (bifrost-dev#9999) and a keyword argument at a modeled call can fail the run (bifrost-dev#9991); the affected-interpreter check needs CPython version evidence (bifrost-dev#3867). Fixed in bifrost.security 2.4.0: bifrost.security.rust.non-https-url no longer reports an http:// literal whose authority is a format placeholder inside a standard formatting macro, such as format!("http://{}", addr) (#339, #340); a literal host before the placeholder, an escaped brace or the same literal outside a formatting macro still report, and a literal nested anywhere inside such a macro call is also excluded. Fixed in bifrost.code-smells 4.0.2: bifrost.correctness.dynamic-evaluation now matches builtin identity instead of the callee name (#376, #379), so member calls such as model.eval(), df.eval(...) and session.exec(...) are no longer reported; a Python eval or exec is reported when python-builtin-identity proves builtins.eval or builtins.exec, a shadowed name leaves the run incomplete with no finding, and a JavaScript or TypeScript eval or Function call is reported when the callee has no lexical binding. ImageMath.eval is no longer reported. All other policies, IDs and consumer requirements are unchanged from rules 0.11.0. This release does not qualify the full policy set or imply complete analysis.
